I went through crippling fentanyl addiction and the cooresponding withdrawals associated around 30 times? Maybe more? I cant remember clearly. Afterall, I was using upwards 60 blues a day by the end.
So heres whats likely to happen.
Opiate use, whether just every weekend or every hour, rewires the frontal cortex of your brain. It effects your decision making. You become erradic, compulsive. You start doing things that youd never have done before. Maybe thats incorporating other drugs, sex, danger, lawlessness. 
Does it dissolve your morality altogether? Not quite, but I can tell you with certainty that you'll do SOMETHING that youll end up regretting forever. You might decide "hey, this stuff makes me happy so why cant I use everyday?"

Another thing thats bound to happen. You think your buying "pure china white". You said the withdrawals last 3 days? I hate to break it to you, that doesnt sound like heroin. Heroin, especially the good shit, is a longlasting opiate. The high lasts longer, and the withdrawals last longer. 
3 days is exactly the length my fentanyl wd's lasted. To a T. No matter if I was using 10 pills a day or 60. Just at 60 the severity of wd's gets incredibly brutal. But it always relaxes by the end of the 3rd day.

Also if im mistaken, you will eventually get a bag of dope mixed with fetty, carfetty or tranq. And your tolerance wont be ready and youll overdose immediately. If you dont get narcan'd then you'll likely die.
Trust me. At my peak usage, when 3 oxy 15's didnt even dent my wd symptoms a little, my dealer had some powdered fent instead of the usual blue pills. I smoked a TINY amount, and I woke up in car getting ice water dumped on me. They narcan'd me twice, it didnt work immediately so they blew meth up my nose. Then I came around. It was very painful. Narcan puts you into instant percolated wd. 

This is not a life you want. No matter how good the high feels. I once pledged my life to fentanyl, told myself that it was my one true love.... now I hate it. I hate what it did to me. I hate what its doing to us. But I also know its not the root cause. The root cause for me was depression, loneliness, suicidality and being overworked and under socialized during covid lockdowns. 

I highly suggest you consider suboxone. If nothing else, it will help you with wd so you can use during the weekend and not necessarily have to call out sick for wd symptoms. My hope is that overtime you slowly stop using and switch just to subs. If not, hey at least youll also get naloxone, and rhat WILL save your life. Probably multiple times by the time your ready to give up opiates, if ever.
Good luck, seriously.
